alice.chen: Heads up — SCIM provisioning to AcmeCorp started failing right after we rolled the IdP cert at ~02:00 UTC. 403s from the SCIM endpoint and KMS decrypt errors in audit logs. Anyone seen this?
ben.platform: Oof. Which errors exactly? can you paste a log line?
alice.chen: Sure — here are a couple of lines from the provisioner:```2026-03-18T02:05:12Z ERROR scim-provisioner user=svc-provision error="http 403" attrs=[...] message="kms:Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException"```and a CloudTrail KMS event:```eventTime: 2026-03-18T02:05:12Z, eventName: Decrypt, errorCode: AccessDeniedException, userIdentity: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/scim-service-role```
carol-idp: Did we also rotate the SCIM OAuth client secret or change the NameID? The timeline matters.
alice.chen: Two relevant changes yesterday: 1) IdP cert rotation 01:47 UTC (SAML). 2) RBAC rename in IAM: former role `scim_writer` -> `scim.service` (manual cleanup patch) ~23:30 UTC. Not sure which clipped this.
sec-oncall: pinging — this smells like KMS key policy or role trust got missed when the role rename happened. Who owns the KMS alias used by the provisioner?
deploy-bot: deploy complete: service/scim-provisioner v2.3.9 by ben.platform at 2026-03-18T01:45:00Z
ben.platform: The provisioner uses alias/aws/redwood-provisioning (customer CMK alias: alias/redwood/provisioning). Did we reassign alias during the key rotation?
alice.chen: We rotated the CMK and created new key, but the old alias `alias/redwood/scim` was still referenced in the DB token metadata. The deploy was updated to `alias/redwood/provisioning`. So stored ciphertexts reference the old key id.
ben.platform: Ah. That explains Decrypt: KMS will fail if the decrypting principal isn't in the new key policy OR the ciphertext was encrypted under a different key id. If ciphertext was created with key A and you killed the alias to A, decrypt will still work if key A exists and policy permits. Did we disable key A?
alice.chen: Looks like key A was scheduled for disable after rotation. There is a line in the KMS audit:```KMS: ScheduleKeyDeletion request for keyId=1234-aaaa at 2026-03-17T23:50:00Z```
carol-idp: If key A is scheduled for deletion, decrypt will fail. We need to cancel deletion or re-encrypt tokens with new key B. Which is less risky depends on rollback surface.
sec-oncall: Immediate steps: 1) cancel deletion of key A if possible and re-enable it; 2) add the `scim-service-role` to key policy for both keys; 3) run a migration to re-encrypt persisted tokens with key B. Do not delete key A until migration completes and we have a retention snapshot.
ben.platform: I'll prepare the policy change. Quick check: who has AWS console perms to cancel deletion? pinging @sec-oncall for cross-account KMS perms.
sec-oncall: I can cancel deletion, but need approval. Alice — do we have business impact? number of failing ops?
alice.chen: Currently provisioning queue is backed up — ~1.2k users pending. AcmeCorp support pinged SRE. It's producing 403 to downstream tenant. Severity S2 for now.
carol-idp: Also check SCIM attribute mapping — if NameID changed during SAML rotate we might be mapping to a different identifier and provisioning is actually 403 due to tenant-level ACL. But KMS log is pretty direct.
ben.platform: I'll push a temporary fix: update provisioner to try decrypt with both key IDs (A and B) and backoff on AccessDenied. That gives us time to migrate. Small patch, can rollback quickly.
alice.chen: Please coordinate — deploy-bot will log. Ben can you also open an encrypted job to re-encrypt tokens? Script should: fetch ciphertext, call KMS decrypt with key A, then re-encrypt with key B, update DB. Dry-run on a small sample first.
ben.platform: Will do. Drafting script now. Also adding log lines to detect failures and retry.
sec-oncall: I'll cancel key deletion now and grant `scim-service-role` decrypt on both keys. Doing it in console — will update when done.
sec-oncall: Done. Cancelled deletion for key A and patched key policy to include role arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/scim-service-role. Waiting for IAM cache to propagate (~1-5 mins).
alice.chen: IAM cache still shows AccessDenied for a few decrypt attempts but some succeed now. Provisioner processed ~120 users successfully after the patch. :thumbsup:
carol-idp: Good. After migration we should run a sanity check: re-run provisioning for a small tenant, validate audit logs show Decrypt events for key B only. Also add a metric for KMS Decrypt failures.
ben.platform: Migration job ran dry-run on 50 items — 0 errors. Scheduling full run in 30m with rate limit to avoid DB write storms.
deploy-bot: deploy started: service/scim-provisioner v2.3.10 by ben.platform at 2026-03-18T03:10:00Z
alice.chen: Full migration finished: re-encrypted 1,237 ciphertexts to key B, updated DB. Queue drained.
sec-oncall: Verified CloudTrail: Decrypt events now reference keyId=B for re-encrypted tokens. No AccessDenied in last 30m. Marking incident as resolved, will file RCA.
carol-idp: RCA items: improve key rotation runbook (explicit step to update stored ciphertext references), add pre-rotation dry-run to detect stored ciphertexts, add metric for KMS Decrypt errors and anomaly alert, and clarify RBAC rename process.
alice.chen: Adding follow-up tickets: audit-log retention check, update RBAC docs, and postmortem with timeline + lessons. Thanks all.
